name: Domestic blue-box trunk seizure
preconditions: answer supervision returned by the far CO
steps: Dial a long-distance number you legitimately reach.
After answer supervision, play 2600 Hz into the audio path for ~700 ms (switch-dependent: 4ESS >=400 ms).
The originating tandem reads far-end on-hook and drops the trunk to a wink/idle while your local loop stays up.
MF-pulse KP + destination digits + ST as if you were an originating tandem.
The tandem routes your new call.
vulnerability_window: Died as trunks migrated SF/MF -> CCIS/SS7. Impractical on major US routes by ~1990; straggler independents into the mid-1990s.
retirement_cause: Out-of-band signaling (CCIS No.6, then SS7): a 2600 Hz tone in the voice path is now just audio.

name: Red-box a fortress phone at an ACTS prompt
preconditions: an ACTS-equipped Bell single-slot (fortress) payphone whose 1700+2200 Hz coin receiver is on the toll switch
steps: Dial a long-distance number from a fortress phone.
Instead of coins, play the 1700+2200 Hz coin-tone bursts into the mouthpiece (quarter = five 33 ms bursts per GR-506-CORE).
ACTS credits the deposit and cuts the call through.
vulnerability_window: Worked ~1978 until ACTS single-slots were retrofitted/replaced 1996-2002.
retirement_cause: Local coin validation in smart payphones (Millennium/COCOT) and T1/robbed-bit trunks stripping in-band ACTS supervision.
